info.title: Stint Partner API
info.description:
Public API for integration partners. This specification covers the endpoints required to look up account resources (sites and roles) and to create employees within the Stint platform.

**Expected flow:**
1. Look up sites and roles using `GET /sites` and `GET /roles` to
   obtain the identifiers needed for assigning an employee to a site.

2. Create the employee with core personal details:
   `POST /employees`

3. Once the employee is created, populate their profile by calling
   the following sub-resource endpoints in any order — each endpoint
   is independent and can be called as data becomes available:
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/employment-information`
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/site-memberships`
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/right-to-work-checks`
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/bank-details`
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/emergency-contact`
   - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/home-address`


**Important:** The initial `POST /employees` call must be made first — it returns the `employeeId` required by all subsequent endpoints. The sub-resource endpoints can then be called in any order.

get.description: Returns all sites belonging to the authenticated account.
Returns all roles belonging to the authenticated account.

post.description:
Creates a new employee record with their core personal details. This must be the first call in the employee creation flow — the returned `id` is required by all subsequent sub-resource endpoints.

Once created, the employee will be in an onboarding state until their profile is completed with employment information, site membership, and other details via the sub-resource endpoints.
Sets the employment information for an employee, including their contract type, pay rate, and expected hours. This information is used for payroll processing and scheduling.

Assigns the employee to a site with a specific role and permission level. Use `GET /sites` and `GET /roles` to look up the identifiers for the site and role you wish to assign.

An employee can be assigned to multiple sites by calling this endpoint once per site. Note that the first site added is regarded as their primary site.

204.description: The site membership was created successfully.

post.summary: Submit a right to work check
post.description:
Submits a right to work check for the employee, including a supporting document. This is required for UK employment compliance.

The document must be provided as a base64-encoded string. Accepted formats include PDF, JPEG, and PNG.

204.description: The right to work check was created successfully.

post.description: Adds the employee's bank details for payroll payments. These details are stored securely and used for salary disbursement.
Adds an emergency contact for the employee. This information is used in the event of a workplace emergency.

204.description: The emergency contact was created successfully.

post.description: Adds the employee's home address. This is used for payroll correspondence and HR records.

204.description: The home address was created successfully.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Scoped API key issued per account. Include as `X-API-Key: <key>` in the request header.

employeeId.name: employeeId
employeeId.description: The unique identifier of the employee, as returned by `POST /employees`.

BadRequest.description: The request body is invalid. The response will include details about which fields failed validation.

Forbidden.description: The API key is valid but does not have the required scope for this operation.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

Conflict.description: The resource already exists. For example, the employee already has employment information, bank details, or a home address recorded.

name.description: The employee's full name, broken down into its component parts.

email.description: The employee's email address. This is used for communication and as a unique identifier for the employee within the account. Must be unique — an error will be returned if an employee with this email address already exists.

dateOfBirth.description: The employee's date of birth. Formatted as an ISO 8601 compliant date (YYYY-MM-DD).

startDate.description: The date the employee is expected to start working. Formatted as an ISO 8601 compliant date (YYYY-MM-DD).

legalStatus.description: The employee's legal working status in the UK. This determines whether the employee is subject to working hour restrictions. `INTERNATIONAL` employees are capped at 20 hours per week during term time in accordance with UK visa regulations. `UK_IRISH` employees have no such restriction.

nationalInsuranceNumber.description: The employee's UK National Insurance number, used for tax and social security purposes. Null when not yet known or not applicable.

contractType.description: The type of employment contract. `FLEXIBLE` indicates the employee works variable hours (e.g. zero-hours or casual contracts). `FIXED` indicates the employee has a guaranteed number of hours per week.

payRate.description: The employee's pay rate in GBP, expressed as a decimal string. For `FLEXIBLE` contracts, this is the hourly rate. For `FIXED` contracts, this is the annual salary. Use a string to avoid floating-point precision issues (e.g. `"12.09"`, not `12.09`).

expectedHours.description: The number of hours the employee is expected to work per week, expressed as a decimal string. For flexible contracts, this represents an indicative average rather than a guarantee.

jobTitle.description: The employee's job title as it should appear on their employment record.

training.description: Whether the employee is currently in a training period. Training employees may be subject to different pay rates or scheduling rules.

siteId.description: The unique identifier of the site to assign the employee to. Use `GET /sites` to retrieve the list of available sites for the account.

roleId.description: The unique identifier of the role the employee will perform at this site. Use `GET /roles` to retrieve the list of available roles for the account.

expiresAt.description: The date and time at which the right to work expires. Formatted as an ISO 8601 compliant date-time. Null when the employee has an indefinite right to work (e.g. a UK or Irish citizen).

document.description: The supporting document for the right to work check.

bankName.description: The name of the bank where the employee holds their account.

accountHolderName.description: The name on the bank account, as it appears on the employee's bank statement. This may differ from the employee's name (e.g. if they use initials).

accountNumber.description: The employee's bank account number. Must be exactly 8 digits.

sortCode.description: The sort code for the employee's bank account. Must be exactly 6 digits, without hyphens (e.g. `"010203"`, not `"01-02-03"`).

addressLine1.example: 210 Drury Lane, Theatre Royal, Catherine Street
addressLine1.description: The full street address, including building number and street name.

postCode.description: The postal code for the address.

town.description: The town or city of the address.

id.description: The unique identifier for the site. This value is stable and will remain consistent across requests.

name.description: A human-readable name for the site, input by the partner. This is subject to change and should not be relied on to stay consistent between requests.

id.description: The unique identifier for the role. This value is stable and will remain consistent across requests.

name.description: A human-readable name for the role, input by the partner. This is subject to change and should not be relied on to stay consistent between requests.

operationalArea.description: The operational area of the role — the area of service (department, team) that the employee works in. This set of values may be extended over time to accommodate the needs of additional partners and industries. Additionally, a role's operational area may change as partners reorganise their departments. Integration partners should handle unrecognised values gracefully and avoid caching this value indefinitely.

middleNames.description: Space-separated middle names, e.g. "Jack Josh". Null when the employee has no middle names.

familyName.description: The employee's family name. Null when the employee does not have a family name.

base64Content.description: The document content, encoded as a base64 string.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the document. Accepted types are `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, and `image/png`.

id.description: The unique identifier of the newly created employee. Use this value as the `employeeId` path parameter in subsequent sub-resource calls.

detail.description: A human-readable description of the error.

servers.description: Sandbox — use this environment for development and testing.
